To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Genetic testing for mutations in cancer predisposition genes has the potential to reduce the burden of cancer in the future, but the clinical utility has yet to be proven.
the identification of cancer predisposing germline mutations is of major importance in clinical practice and that the role of clinical geneticists is essential in this process.

1)  The number of hereditary cancer genes has been rapidly growing, and the clinical utility of many of them is still unclear. 2)  Clinical geneticists are ideally placed to provide genetic counselling, to perform pedigree analysis, and to select patients and families who are eligible for genetic testing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical and genetic aspects of familial cancer, and the role of the clinical geneticist in the management of hereditary cancer
the identification of cancer predisposing gene mutations and the subsequent clinical and molecular characterization of these patients.

the clinical utility of genetic testing and risk reducing interventions in hereditary cancer, and with the development of new strategies for cancer prevention in carriers of cancer susceptibility mutations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
clinical geneticists are the ideal professionals for hereditary cancer management and research.
the clinical geneticists are the key players in this field, but that they need to be part of a multidisciplinary team to be successful.
genetic testing for cancer predisposing genes is not a panacea but that it is a strong tool to improve the care for patients and families with hereditary cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are in the process of developing the field of clinical cancer genetics, and that we have a major impact on cancer care.
we are in a transition period from the discovery of genes to the translation of the findings to clinical applications.

we need to work on the following points:
To further develop and improve the clinical and molecular genetic services for hereditary cancer patients and their families. 
To improve the quality of clinical genetic testing for cancer predisposing mutations and to develop guidelines for the clinical interpretation and reporting of genetic test results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clinical geneticists are key players in the management of hereditary cancer.

genetic testing for hereditary breast cancer should be performed by a clinical geneticist, and that the geneticist should be involved in the follow up of patients with mutations and in the counselling of family members.
clinical geneticists are essential for the success of hereditary cancer management and research, and that their role is not only to counsel patients and families and to perform genetic testing.
